no recipe text is copied. These are recommendations for Aly and Noor to accept, not yet the app's data.

## Cooking tips from Reddit and YouTube comments

**R001 Chicken Biryani (Extreme)**

- Thread asking for a foolproof biryani. One user calls a Food Fusion Karachi-style masala biryani video the best. Others marinate the chicken in Shan masala and yogurt. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- Users share their own home methods. No single website or channel stands out. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- Advice: biryani is basically a thick chicken masala layered with rice, and packet biryani masala is an accepted shortcut. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)

**R002 Chicken Yakhni Pulao**

- Discussion of which meat to buy for pulao. One commenter recommends any Kun Foods recipe for Urdu speakers and explains boiling the rice in the stock, then cooking it on dum (sealed, low heat). (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- A user posts their own whole-spice yakhni recipe. No agreement on a best source. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- Very positive. People who made it several times say it comes out flavourful every time. A top-liked tip adds a Shan yakhni pulao packet or a stock cube to the stock. Based on the top ~20 comments, read 2026-10-04.

**R003 Red Beans (Lal Lobia Masala)**

- Users say to avoid canned beans. Pressure-cook dried beans with whole spices and keep the cooking water. Cook the onions well and add kasuri methi near the end.
- Mash a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy. Don't mash too many or it turns to pulp.
- Without a pressure cooker: add soaked beans to boiling water, cover, and start checking after 30-45 minutes until they are fork-tender.

**R004 Chicken Karahi (Fire)**

- Users stress using plenty of oil, fresh ginger-garlic rather than paste, and frying the chicken before adding tomatoes. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- Advice: cook the tomatoes down until the oil separates, add green chillies and ginger near the end, and stir in yogurt if it is too spicy. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- The poster followed a YouTube recipe. Their hotter stove dried out the masala, so they had to keep adding water. They used breast instead of thigh. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)

**R005 Chicken Qorma**

- Someone asks for a quick qorma recipe. The replies were not visible in the snippet. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- Replies point to British curry-house korma, which is not Pakistani qorma. A reminder to avoid the creamy, sweet restaurant style for this app. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- Positive. Viewers like the short, straight-to-the-point format and say their families enjoyed it. Few detailed tips. Based on the top ~20 comments, read 2026-10-04.

**R006a Daal Chana (Masala)**

- Main warning: soak chana dal first and cook it until very soft, then mash or partly blend it. Many recipes skip this step.
- One user found a one-hour soak was not enough. Others say 12-15 minutes at high pressure works.
- If soaked dal still won't break down, users suggest a pinch of baking soda. Old dal can stay hard no matter what.

**R006b Daal Mash with Tadka**

- The poster boils the lentils to about 90% done so they stay slightly firm, then finishes them in the masala. This keeps the grains separate.
- Photo of a first attempt. Commenters praised the dhaba look, and one mentioned Shahi Daal Mash as a variation.
- Khari (dry) style: soak the daal 5-6 hours, then cook it covered on low heat with little water.

**R006c Daal Masoor (Malka) - split red lentils**

- For a bland first red-lentil dal, the advice was a proper hot-oil cumin tempering poured in at the end. Avoid adding both canned tomatoes and broth, which dilute the flavour.
- Masoor is the fastest dal to cook. For a tadka-style dal, cook the dal and temper the spices separately.
- Home-style tip: boil the red lentils with turmeric and salt to the consistency you want, then add a simple tarka. Heavy masala makes it taste like curry instead of daal.

**R007 Beef Salan (Aloo Gosht, Delhi style)**

- Beef aloo gosht made in an Instant Pot. The poster said the beef was less tender than they wanted but it tasted good, which suggests beef needs more pressure time. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- If the shorba (gravy) is too thin, simmer it uncovered on the stove to thicken it. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- Positive. Called easy and relaxed to make. One viewer used a pressure cooker and added bay leaf and cinnamon, with good results. Based on the top ~20 comments, read 2026-10-04.

**R008 Shami Kabab**

- The poster's kababs kept falling apart in the pan. Advice: add an egg to the mixture and dip the kababs in beaten egg too. Use about equal meat and chana daal. Don't let the pressure cooker run dry. Fry in hot oil, not cold. Boil potatoes in big chunks so they hold less water. A little flour or besan helps bind. Some prefer shredding the meat by hand or on a sil-batta instead of a grinder for better texture.
- A first-timer's kababs broke when flipped. Replies suggest a little flour or breadcrumbs to bind them.
- A family recipe post. Meat is pressure-cooked with chana daal, flavoured with ginger, garlic, green chilli, mint and garam masala, then shallow fried. Replies were only positive.

**R009 Chicken Manchurian**

- Someone asked for a 2-person Manchurian recipe; replies pointed to Tea for Turmeric's blog and to the Taste Show YouTube video (I_6aMZwf9CU, 21.2M views, Indo-Chinese style), the latter with a 'just follow it' endorsement.
- Chilli garlic ketchup recommended over plain tomato ketchup for more kick; plain ketchup gives a sweeter, milder result.
- Mostly compliments; one commenter said their homemade attempt tasted 'a bit weird' and asked which sauces to use, which suggests the sauce balance is the tricky part.

**R010 Chinese Fried Rice**

- A commenter who did not expect to like Pakistani fried rice said basmati, instead of jasmine or short-grain rice, gives it a delicate flavour.
- Users say most Pakistani homes want separate, fluffy grains ('khilay khilay') and use basmati for fried rice and pulao. Sella is mostly kept for biryani.
- A first-timer's well-received shrimp fried rice was made from a Food Fusion recipe.

**R011 One Pot Spicy Pasta**

- Users warn that many local Pakistani pasta brands turn mushy. Bake Parlor, Mario, Nature's Own and Reggia were named as better options, or imported packs (around Rs 500).
- Most suggest making your own sauce. Salman's and Trandoz jars were rated decent bases; store sauces usually need extra seasoning. One tip: season the sauce slightly saltier, spicier and tangier than you want, because the pasta dilutes it.
- Pantry ideas for desi pasta: a garlic, chilli, soy, vinegar and lemon toss; chilli-oil aglio e olio; or a little yogurt in place of cheese to balance tomato sauce.

**R012 Chicken Macaroni (Korma-style)**

- Commenters prefer desi-style macaroni to Western versions. The poster's flavourings were chilli powder, vinegar, soy, macaroni masala and ketchup with capsicum, carrot and onion; one person suggested a little achaar for extra desi flavour.
- The pasta-brand warnings apply here too: some local elbow macaroni goes mushy; Bake Parlor and imported brands were preferred.
- Many 'tried it, turned out delicious' comments in Urdu and English; a top comment lists boiling steps. Lots of off-topic prayer comments. Desi-Chinese style, not korma.

**R013 Bhindi (Masala Aloo Bhindi)**

- How to stop the slime: wash and fully dry the okra before cutting, or air-dry the slices. Fry on high heat, stirring, until the stickiness goes. Add salt late. Lemon or another sour ingredient helps.
- Keep moisture out: cook uncovered, add salt last, and use lemon, vinegar or yogurt to cut slime. Some say frozen okra works straight from the freezer on medium-high heat. Boiled potato soaks up gumminess.
- For beginners: dry the okra, and cut it bigger or lengthwise so it releases less slime. Half-fry the potatoes before adding the okra. Cut back the chilli for people who can't take heat.

**R014 Gobi Masala (Dhaba Style)**

- Mushy gobi: cook it less and add the cauliflower later. Many recipes pre-fry or blanch the florets and add them near the end.
- Cut the potatoes small and don't crowd the pan. One user warns that boiling the cauliflower first turns it to mush. Another found Swasthi's cooking times too short and wished they had par-boiled. For a dry version, Priya Krishna's roasted aloo gobi (Bon Appetit) is suggested.
- People who disliked gobi say this recipe changed their mind. A 10-year-old made it successfully. Commenters praise the step-by-step explanation, and several made it 2-3 times. Pakistani dhaba style, 8:41.

**R015 Karela (Qeema Karelay)**

- Lots of love for keema karelay. Commenters explain 'band' karelay: seeds removed, stuffed with qeema and tied shut with thread. Several say well-made karela is barely bitter.
- To cut bitterness: peel, slit and remove the seeds, then salt for a few hours or overnight. Rinse, squeeze hard and fry. Some skip salting because they like the bitterness.
- Asks whether salting removes nutrients. Replies say the loss is small and that some bitterness is the point of the dish.

**R016 Aalu (Masala Aloo)**

- For dry aloo that turns out bland or mushy: cut the potatoes small and cook uncovered on medium, letting them brown a little. Wash the cut potatoes. Users disagree on waxy versus starchy potatoes. Fry the jeera in oil rather than boiling it with the potatoes.
- Several people tried it and called it amazing or the best. The rest is generic praise. I saw no complaints.

**R017 Qeema (Dhaba Style Aloo Qeema)**

- A popular qeema post (228 upvotes). The poster's tip: bhuno (stir-fry) the qeema a lot, until it has a fried texture, before adding tomatoes. They used about half a packet of Shan keema masala. Others call aloo qeema an underrated home staple.
- For chewy keema: don't boil the mince first. Brown it directly in the masala, add salt later and don't overcook. Marinating in yogurt and spices also helps.
- A recipe-share post linking to jamilghar.com. Little discussion, and only positive replies.

**R018 Beef Nihari**

- A first-timer asks which YouTube cook to trust for nihari. The replies were not visible in the snippet. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- Discussion of homemade nihari masala. One user cuts the chilli for a milder dish and adds a little water so the masala does not burn. (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)
- The poster made slow-cooked beef shank nihari using a Tea for Turmeric recipe (the Instant Pot version). (Reddit cannot be fetched directly; summary from search-result snippet only.)

**R019 Khichri (Spicy Fried Khichdi)**

- Popular additions: a final tarka of onion, tomato, chillies, garlic and ginger, plus extra ghee on top. Some mix several dals with rice in equal parts.
- To keep some texture, lightly fry the moong in the cumin tadka before adding water.
- Adjust the water for the consistency you want, then finish with a small ghee or mustard-oil tadka with cumin and hing.

**R020 Saag (Sarson Ka Saag)**

- Saag greens can be bitter. Blanching them helps remove the bitterness.
- Remove tough stems, which add bitterness, and caramelise the onions to balance the bitter greens.
- Punjabi families use mustard greens, spinach, fenugreek and bathua. Users warn that dill does not suit sarson ka saag.

## Limits

- Researched by four Claude agents on 2026-10-04. View and like counts were read from each YouTube watch page; star ratings and rating counts from each recipe page's embedded rating data.
- Reddit blocks direct access, so Reddit feedback comes from search snippets or third-party archives (PullPush, Arctic Shift); scores may be out of date, and most threads are general or Indian rather than Pakistani.
- YouTube comments: the top 15 to 40 comments per main video were read; total comment counts were not collected.
- Food Fusion pages show no star ratings or servings. Masala TV pages all show the same 5.0 from 235, which looks like a placeholder and was treated as unreliable.
- R006c was redone for split red masoor, because Noor's recipe (300 g masoor daal, curry leaves, lemon, 40 min) is the split red lentil; the current Food Fusion links use whole black masoor.
- External links and numbers change over time; recheck before relying on them.
